label_correction_reason: The original contract never excluded ordinary contiguous torch.Tensor objects carrying the lazy-negative flag. case_108 passes their raw storage pointers to Triton without resolving that flag, so initial trust qualification omitted legal logical values. Old source, contract and experimental records are preserved; a new case_111 resolves all four input tensors before pointer use. This corrects the original label, not an input-dependent label policy.
classification: targeted wrapper-contract audit and synthetic repair of the T4-adapted Liger backward case
repair: Resolve PyTorch lazy-negative views on x, weight, dy, rstd. resolve_neg() materializes logical values only when necessary and preserves the supplied input tensors. FP16/FP32 inputs are real-valued, so no conjugate resolution is required.
public_semantic_diff:
--- case_108/kernel.py
+++ case_111/kernel.py
@@ -58,6 +58,7 @@
 
 def run(x, weight, dy, rstd):
     """Return (dx: FP16[M,N], dw: FP32[N]); preserve all inputs."""
+    x, weight, dy, rstd = (t.resolve_neg() for t in (x, weight, dy, rstd))
     m, n = x.shape
     assert x.is_cuda and x.is_contiguous() and dy.is_contiguous()
     assert weight.is_contiguous() and rstd.is_contiguous()
validation_plan: Repeat the original 18 ordinary probes for case_111, then test single-input and simultaneous lazy-negative flags on legal row and block shapes against an independent NumPy oracle of resolved logical values. case_108 rejection requires actual GPU error on a legal flagged tensor.
